title: Every automated test record gets an outcome, and one that did not run is failed with did not run
when: With a fixture repository whose spec has three automated test records and one that is not automated yet, and suites' output in which two of the automated tests ran: assure record runs at the commit checked out.
then: It exits 0, and the predicate holds one outcome for each automated test record, in ID order. The test that did not run is failed with the detail did not run. The record that is not automated yet has no outcome.

title: The suites job fails for a missing, extra, cut or incomplete part, and for a failed test or package of any name
when: The test runs the join step and the failure check of the proof run workflow's suites job with bash and pipefail on artifact folders of the five parts: a whole set, and sets with a missing part, an extra part, a cut JSON line, a listed package with no result, a root package in no part, no Python output, a failed Go test whose name has no ID, a failed package, and a failed Python test whose name has no ID. It also reads how the tests job splits cmd/stego.
then: The whole set joins and passes. Each set with a missing, extra, cut or incomplete part fails the join, so no proof run is recorded or attested. Each set with a failed test or package, of any name, joins and then fails the suites job. The stego-build part selects cmd/stego's tests with go test -run and the stego part leaves them out with go test -skip, by the same pattern, so each test runs in exactly one part.

title: Outcomes come from Go and Python subtests by the ID in their names, and a test with no ID is ignored
when: The Python runner runs a suite with a passing subtest that carries an ID and a failing subtest that carries none. The go test -json output has a passing and a failing subtest with IDs, and a failing subtest with no ID. assure record reads both.
then: The outcome of each automated test record is that of the subtest that carries its ID: passed, failed and passed. The failing tests with no ID give no outcome and do not refuse the run.

title: An outcome for an ID that is not a test record refuses the run, and no predicate is written
when: assure record reads go test -json output with a subtest that carries an ID that is not a test record in the spec at the commit.
then: It exits non-zero, names the ID, and writes no predicate and no step output.

title: The subject is the full commit checked out, and a short ID, a branch or another commit is refused
when: With a fixture repository at its second commit: assure record runs with a short ID, with the name of the branch checked out, with the first commit, and then with the full commit checked out. The attest job's subject step of proof-run.yml runs for that commit.
then: The first three runs exit non-zero and write nothing. The last writes a predicate about the commit checked out, and the subject step names that commit as the subject, with the SHA-256 of its ID as the digest.

title: A tree with uncommitted changes is refused, also when git status hides them
when: assure record runs in fixture repositories with a changed file, a staged change, an untracked file, a change hidden by skip-worktree, an automated test record added to the spec and hidden by assume-unchanged, an untracked file hidden by info/exclude, an untracked file hidden by the user's excludes file, another commit's tree shown by a replace ref, a same-size change hidden by minimal stat checks, and a new file hidden by an untracked .gitignore that ignores itself. Each hidden case first shows that git status shows no change.
then: Each run exits non-zero, says that the tree has uncommitted changes, and writes nothing.

title: Only the trusted workflow's attestation job signs the proof run, it runs no repository code, and CI commits no evidence file
when: Reads the proof-run.yml workflow, and reads it key by key: the workflow, and the attest job with every key and every step with each of its keys and values, in order, against the keys, steps and values allowed. Runs its subject step with a branch name, and its predicate check step with a predicate about the commit and with one about another commit. Then assure record runs as a job of another workflow, and then with a predicate file in the repository.
then: The workflow and its suites job may only read the repository, and the workflow has only its allowed keys and no environment but the commit and the Lathe pin. Of the jobs that sign a proof run, only the attest job may write an identity token and attestations. The attest job is exactly: needs the suites job, may only get an identity token and write attestations, has no condition, container or defaults, and its four steps: download the proof run, check that it is about the commit, name the commit as the subject, and sign it with actions/attest at the proof run predicate type with the subject that the subject step names; it checks out and runs no code of the repository. Every action is pinned to a commit, and no step commits or pushes. The suites job checks out the pull request head or the commit pushed and records the proof run at it, under the runner's temporary folder, with assure built in the base checkout's cmd/assure, which is the pull request's base commit or the commit pushed, with workspace mode off, into a folder under the runner's temporary folder that the build step makes read-only, before any step runs code of the change, and after a Go setup that restores no cache. The subject step refuses a branch, and the predicate check refuses a predicate about another commit. Both runs of assure record exit non-zero, write nothing, and leave the repository with no change.

title: A change under which an obligation falls is refused, and one that only adds unbuilt, unproved obligations passes
when: With a fixture repository whose base head has two invariants built and proved, one only designed and a constraint only designed: assure gate change runs for a change that adds an invariant with no rule and no test, and then for a change that adds it and also removes the rules' file and one test record, each with a passed proof run at its commit.
then: The first change passes with no reason, and the decision gives its coverage. The second exits non-zero and names each obligation that fell with its share: both invariants from built, and one also from proved.

title: A change is not gated when Lathe finds an error in the spec at the base head or at the change
when: assure gate change runs, with a passed proof run, for a change that drops every rule, test record and rules file against a base head whose spec has a dangling test record, and then for a change with that dangling test record against a clean base head.
then: Each run exits 2, prints no decision, and names the error Lathe finds, so a spec with errors is never read as an empty coverage.

title: A change that retires an obligation to a successor with each standing it had at the base passes, and the decision reports the retirement
when: With a fixture repository whose base head has two invariants built and proved, one only designed and a constraint only designed: assure gate change runs, with a passed proof run at its commit, for a change that renames a built and proved invariant, with its rule, test record and test, and adds a retirement that names the old invariant with the new one as its successor.
then: The change passes with no reason, and the decision reports the retirement as retirement, its ID, the retired invariant and succeeded by the new invariant.

title: A change whose retirement names a successor without a standing the retired obligation had at the base is refused, and the reason names the retirement
when: With the same fixture repository: assure gate change runs, with a passed proof run at its commit, for a change that renames a built and proved invariant with its rule but removes its test record and test, and adds a retirement that names the old invariant with the new one as its successor.
then: The change exits non-zero with one reason: the old invariant is retired by the retirement, but its successor, the new invariant, is not proved. The decision reports no retirement as followed.

title: A retirement with no successor admits the removal of the obligation it names, and a removal that no retirement names is still refused
when: With the same fixture repository: assure gate change runs, with a passed proof run at its commit, for a change that removes the invariant that is only designed and adds a retirement with no successor that names it; then for a change that also removes the constraint, which no retirement names.
then: The first change passes with no reason, and the decision reports that the retirement's invariant has no successor. The second exits non-zero with one reason, that the constraint is absent at the change and was designed at the base, and the decision still reports the retirement.

title: A change with no verified proof run at its commit, or with an automated test record not passed there, is refused
when: assure gate change runs for one change with a store that keeps no attestation; one forged attestation and one about another commit; a proof run signed at another pull request's ref; a proof run with a failed test and a test with no outcome; one with a skipped test; and one in which every automated test passed.
then: Each run but the last exits non-zero. With no proof run that verifies, the reason says there is no verified proof run at the commit and why each attestation is refused. Otherwise each test record that did not pass is named with its result. The last run passes.

title: A refusal names each obligation that fell with its share and each test record that did not pass, and exits non-zero
when: assure gate change runs, with the job's step summary file set, for a change that removes the rules' file, a test record and an invariant, and whose proof run has the remaining automated test failed. Then it runs, with another step summary file, for a change whose spec has a test record that names a file that does not exist. Then it runs with that summary file set and no --base.
then: It exits non-zero and says the change is refused. The reasons are each on a line of their own: each obligation that fell, with each share it fell from, the invariant the change removes as absent at the change with the share it had at the base, and the failed test record. The step summary holds the same decision, and the repository has no change. For the change with the broken spec it exits 2 and prints no decision, and the other step summary holds one line that says no decision was reached and names Lathe's error. With no --base it exits 2, and the summary holds one line that says no decision was reached because the gate is called wrongly.

title: The same commit, base and proof run give the same decision and reasons in the same order
when: assure gate change runs twice for a change refused for five reasons, with a change-grade proof run and a forged one; then a third time with the store giving the attestations in the other order and with changes in the working tree.
then: The three runs give the same exit code and the same decision, byte for byte.

title: A change is refused for a code-standard fault the base head does not have, and a fault the base has is reported, not refused
when: With a fixture repository whose base head has two code-standard faults, a Go file no record names and a rule record whose identifier its file does not declare, and a passed proof run at each change: assure gate change runs for a change that adds another Go file no record names, for a change that keeps the base's faults, for a change under which the rule record names another identifier its file does not declare, and for a change that removes the unnamed file of the base.
then: The first change exits 1 and names the new file with its rule and key as the one reason; its code faults list all three by rule and key, the new one as not at base and the others as present at base. The second change passes and reports both faults of the base as present at base. The third passes: the fault keeps its rule and key, and is reported with its new reason as present at base. The fourth passes and reports only the fault that remains.

title: A proof run signed at the change's own ref counts only while the workflows folder is the base's, and one signed at main counts for any tree
when: assure gate change runs for a change that alters, adds and removes a workflow file, first with a passed proof run signed at the change's own ref, then with one signed at main; then for a change that leaves the workflows folder as the base has it, with a passed proof run signed at its own ref.
then: The first run is refused: no verified proof run, because the change alters the workflows folder, and each file that differs is named. The second and third runs pass.

title: A proof run signed at the change's own ref by a run at a merge of another commit, or into another branch, is refused
when: In a fixture repository, a pull request's earlier head alters the proof run workflow and its later head leaves the workflows folder as the base has it. assure gate change runs for the later head with a passed proof run signed at the change's own ref by a run at the merge commit of the earlier head; then by a run at the later head itself, which is no merge commit; then by a run at a commit that the provider does not keep; then by a run at the merge commit of the later head into the earlier head, as for a pull request whose base was another branch before it was retargeted; then by a run at the merge commit of the later head. The fixture store gives the parents of each commit as GitHub's git commits API does.
then: The first four runs are refused with exactly one reason: no verified proof run, because the run's commit is not a merge commit whose second parent is the later head, with the parents the provider gives, or, for the fourth, because the merge commit's first parent is not the base head. The last run passes.

title: The gate job builds assure from the base commit only, and runs it in the change's checkout with the pinned Lathe, which the change cannot alter
when: Reads the proof run workflow, its gate job and every key of the job and its steps, and compares the job with the expected job that the test holds. Then, in a fixture repository, assure gate change runs with a Lathe that a run on the change's tree rewrites, so that a run of the rewritten Lathe gives no coverage, for a change that rewrites it and has a passed proof run; then it runs again with the rewritten Lathe.
then: The gate job is exactly the expected job: each key of the job, and each step in order with each of its keys (run, with, env, uses, working-directory, if, shell and any other), so that no text that shell quoting hides can enter it; the workflow runs only on a push to main, a pull request and by hand. In that job: the workflow and the job have no defaults and no key that lets a failed step pass, and the job has no environment of its own; the workflow's environment is only the change's commit and LATHE_REF, a full commit. The job runs on each pull request unless the run is cancelled, may only read the repository, uses only the checkout, setup-go and setup-node actions, and restores no cache. Between the change's checkout and the base's, one step finds the base: the merge commit's first parent, checked to descend from the payload base and lie on the base branch, with a check that the merge commit's second parent is the change's head; it runs only git, in the change's checkout, and gives the base as its output. The job checks out exactly three things: the change's commit with its full history into stego, Lathe at LATHE_REF, and the base that it found into a folder of its own, with no other input, so it never builds the gate from the head, the merge commit, or a base with no checks. Each step sets only the environment it needs, by its exact value: workspace mode off for the build, and the base and the token for the gate. The only go command of the job builds assure in the base's cmd/assure, after that checkout, into the runner's temporary folder. No step but the gate and the step that finds the base runs in or names the change's checkout, runs git, or runs a package manager, an interpreter or a script outside Lathe's folder, and every step before the gate runs. Right before the gate, a step makes Lathe and the built binary read-only. The gate step runs exactly that binary in the change's checkout, for the change's commit against the base that the job found, with one --lathe that names the Lathe built from LATHE_REF, and with only the base and the token in its environment. The first gate run passes, and the change's run did rewrite the Lathe: the base was measured before it. The second run gives no decision, as the rewritten Lathe cannot measure the base.

title: A release is refused while any obligation is not designed, built and proved, and each such obligation is named
when: With a fixture repository and a passed proof run signed at main at each commit: assure gate release runs at a commit whose spec has an obligation Lathe counts as neither built nor proved and one it counts as not proved, and then at a commit whose every obligation is designed, built and proved.
then: The first decision is refused, gives the coverage at the commit, names each obligation with each share it does not have (one not proved, the other not built and not proved), and no decision predicate is written. The fully proved commit passes.
notes: Measures ST-BO07: the share of obligations designed, built and proved is what this gate reads, and a release passes only at 100%.

title: A release commit with no verified proof run, or with an automated test record not passed there, is refused
when: With a fixture repository whose release commit is fully proved: assure gate release runs with a store that keeps no attestation; with a forged attestation; with a proof run signed at main in which a test failed and one has no outcome; with one in which a test was skipped; and with one in which every automated test passed.
then: Each run but the last exits 1 and writes no predicate. With no proof run that verifies, the reason says there is no verified proof run at the commit and why. Otherwise each test record that did not pass is named with its result. The last run passes.

title: The release gate job runs on a push to main, and only the attest-release job, which runs no repository code, signs a passed decision with the commit as subject
when: Reads proof-run.yml key by key: the workflow, and the gate-release and attest-release jobs with every key of each job and every step with each of its keys and values, in order, against the keys, steps and values allowed. Runs the gate-release job's gate step with an assure that exits 0, 1, 2 and 3. Runs the attest-release job's subject step for a commit and for a branch name, and its predicate check step with a passed release decision about the commit, one about another commit, a refused one, one of the change gate and one with no kind.
then: The workflow has only its allowed keys, read-only permissions and no environment but the commit and the Lathe pin. The gate-release job is exactly: needs the attest job, runs on each push to main also when the suites or the attest job fail, may only read the repository, gives the gate step's output passed as its own, and its nine steps: check out the commit with its full history and the pinned Lathe, set up Go with no cache and Node, build Lathe, build assure, remove the Go problem matcher, run assure gate release with the commit, a predicate under the runner's temporary folder and the Lathe the workflow builds, and upload the predicate only when passed is true; no other step has a condition or goes on after an error. The gate step gives passed=true for exit 0, ends green with passed=false for a refused release (exit 1), and fails with no output for exit 2 or 3. Every action is pinned to a commit. Only the attest and attest-release jobs may get an identity token or write attestations. The attest-release job is exactly: needs the gate-release job and runs only when its output passed is true, may only get an identity token and write attestations, has no container or defaults, and its four steps: download the predicate, check it, name the commit as the subject, and sign it with actions/attest at the release-decision predicate type; it checks out and runs no code of the repository. The subject step names the commit as the subject with the SHA-256 of its ID as the digest and refuses the branch, and the check accepts only the passed release decision about the commit.

title: A release commit whose tree has a code-standard fault is refused, and each fault is named with its file and rule
when: With a fixture repository whose release commit is fully proved, and a passed proof run signed at main: assure gate release runs at a commit that adds a Go file no record names and names, in a rule record, an identifier that the rule's file does not declare.
then: It exits 1 and writes no predicate. The decision gives a coverage of 100% for each share, lists both faults in its code faults with the file and the rule, ST-STD-CODE-R02 before ST-STD-CODE-R05, and names each as a reason with its file, the rule and its key.

title: A release takes only a proof run signed at main, and one signed at any other ref is refused with the ref named
when: With a fixture repository whose release commit is fully proved: assure gate release runs with a passed proof run signed at a pull request's ref, then with one signed at another branch, then with both one signed at the pull request's ref and one signed at main.
then: The first two runs exit 1, write no predicate, and say that there is no verified proof run at the commit because the attestation is signed at that ref, not at refs/heads/main. The third run passes, and its decision rests on the proof run signed at main.

title: The ledger comes from verified attestations and the committed spec, and no file of the working tree changes it
when: With a fixture repository of five commits and a store that keeps proof run attestations for four of them, one of which fails verification: assure ledger runs for the newest commit with a clean tree; then with the working tree at the oldest commit, its spec changed and evidence files that say every test passed; then with a store that keeps no attestation; then for a commit with no spec, with a short commit ID, with no commit and with a depth of zero.
then: The first two runs print the same ledger, byte for byte, from the committed spec and the verified attestations, and the repository has no change. With no attestation every result is none, no test record has passed, and it exits 1. The commit with no spec and the wrong calls exit 2 and print no ledger.

title: Each test record shows its state, its result at the commit and the newest commit a verified proof run passed it at, within the depth
when: With a fixture repository of five commits whose newest has a proof run with one automated test failed, the next none, the next one that fails verification and the next both automated tests passed: assure ledger runs for the newest commit twice, then with --depth 2, then for a commit whose proof run passed every test, then with a store in which a test never passed.
then: Each line gives the test record, its state, its result at the commit and the newest commit it passed at; the walk passes over the commit with no attestation, asks for each commit once, and stops where every automated test has passed. The two runs give the same text. With --depth 2 the failed test says not within 2 commits. When every automated test passed it exits 0 and lists only the manual test as not passed; otherwise it exits 1. A test that never passed makes the walk reach the root commit.

title: An attestation that fails verification gives no result at its commit, and the ledger says why
when: With the history of ST-ASR-UC04-R02-T01 and the attestation at the newest commit forged: assure ledger runs for that commit. Then, with change-grade proof runs signed at a pull request's ref: it runs for a change, without and with GITHUB_REF set to that ref; for a commit made as a pull request's merge ref, whose first parent is main's head, with a change-grade attestation, one signed at main by a run at another commit and one signed at a branch at commit 4; for a change that alters a workflow file, also with two statements signed at that ref whose certificates name another source repository and another source ref; and with --base or --main naming the commit itself (the reviewer's spoof).
then: An attestation that is unverifiable or change grade shows as none, with the reason. At the forged commit every result is none, the proof run line says none is verified at release grade, and a line for that commit and one for the forged ancestor give the verifier's reason; the passes come from the older verified proof run, and it exits 1. Each change-grade attestation, at the commit or at an ancestor, is listed as change grade at its ref, counting only in its own gate, and gives no result, with GITHUB_REF set or not; it exits 1. For the merge ref the last passes come from the release-grade proof runs of its first-parent history, and the attestation signed at main by a run at another commit and the one at a branch are refused with their reasons. The two statements whose certificates name another source are refused with that reason, not listed as change grade. --base and --main are not flags of assure ledger: it exits 2 and prints no ledger.

title: A failed resolution leaves go.mod and go.sum as they were
when: With a project that stego apply made and stego deps resolved: a source file imports a module that does not exist, and stego deps runs.
then: stego deps fails; go.mod and go.sum keep their bytes, and no apply journal is left.

title: An interrupted resolution leaves the module files as they were, or as resolved
when: With a project that stego apply made, and the resolved pair of go.mod and go.sum known: the old pair is restored and stego deps runs seven times, each time with an interrupt signal after a longer delay, and stego recover runs when stego deps asks for recovery.
then: At least one run is interrupted; after each run no apply journal is left, and go.mod and go.sum are together either the old pair or the resolved pair.
notes: The interrupt reaches a run at a point that depends on timing. The in-package test ST-BLD-INV01-T interrupts each point of the apply journal by injection.

title: A saved overlay flag and ambient GOFLAGS cannot change what resolution reads
when: With a resolved project, a local module that a saved -overlay flag would import, a Go configuration file that saves that flag and turns the module proxy off, and an invalid ambient GOFLAGS: stego deps runs.
then: The overlay's import never reaches go.mod, and the source is unchanged.

title: Resolution ignores an ambient vendor flag and a missing go.work
when: With a project that stego apply made, a local replace directive, GOFLAGS=-mod=vendor and GOWORK naming a missing file: stego deps runs twice.
then: Both runs succeed, give the same go.mod, and keep the local replacement.

title: Resolution refuses out-of-date generated code and names apply
when: With a project whose code was never applied, and then with a project whose declaration changed after apply: stego deps runs.
then: Each run fails, the error names stego apply, and no project file changes.

title: A downloaded cache holds only the zips whose hashes go.sum states
when: With a committed module that needs one small module, its hash in go.sum, and the pinned Go SDK: stego build download runs.
then: The cache holds exactly one zip, that of the module go.sum states.
notes: It needs the Go SDK that STEGO pins: STEGO_TEST_PINNED_GO names its bin/go, else the SDK that runs the test is used, and the test skips when STEGO refuses that SDK as not the pinned one. A skip is not a pass.

title: A zip whose hash differs from go.sum stops the download, which names both hashes
when: With a committed module whose go.sum states a wrong hash for its one dependency, and the pinned Go SDK: stego build download runs.
then: The download fails, names the module, its version, the hash go.sum states and the hash of the zip, and leaves nothing in the parent folder.
notes: It needs the Go SDK that STEGO pins: STEGO_TEST_PINNED_GO names its bin/go, else the SDK that runs the test is used, and the test skips when STEGO refuses that SDK as not the pinned one. A skip is not a pass.

title: The cache record lists each module by path, version and hash, and the revision it serves
when: With a committed module that needs one small module, and the pinned Go SDK: stego build download runs.
then: module-cache.json names the commit and lists the one module with its path, its version and the hash go.sum states.
notes: It needs the Go SDK that STEGO pins: STEGO_TEST_PINNED_GO names its bin/go, else the SDK that runs the test is used, and the test skips when STEGO refuses that SDK as not the pinned one. A skip is not a pass.

title: A module the proxy cannot supply stops the download, which names it and leaves nothing
when: With a committed module that needs a module the module proxy cannot supply, and the pinned Go SDK: stego build download runs.
then: The download fails, names that module and its version, and leaves no cache folder, no record and no work folder.
notes: It needs the Go SDK that STEGO pins: STEGO_TEST_PINNED_GO names its bin/go, else the SDK that runs the test is used, and the test skips when STEGO refuses that SDK as not the pinned one. A skip is not a pass.

title: An interrupted download leaves no cache folder and no record
when: With a committed module that needs one small module, and the pinned Go SDK: stego build download runs six times, each time with an interrupt signal after a longer delay.
then: At least one download is interrupted. Each interrupted download fails and leaves nothing in its parent folder; each complete one leaves the cache folder with its record.
notes: The interrupt reaches a download at a point that depends on timing. It needs the Go SDK that STEGO pins: STEGO_TEST_PINNED_GO names its bin/go, else the SDK that runs the test is used, and the test skips when STEGO refuses that SDK as not the pinned one. A skip is not a pass.

title: A target that exists or overlaps, or an SDK that is not pinned, is refused by name before any work
when: With a source folder and a fake Go SDK: stego build download runs with a target that exists, a target inside the source, a target inside the SDK, and then with a new target and the fake SDK.
then: Each run is refused and names the target or the SDK, with what it found and what it expected, and no file or folder is made, so no command and no network connection ran.

title: A target with ./ and a file:// source are taken, and a bad flag is refused by its name and value
when: With a source folder and a fake Go SDK: stego build download runs with the target ./cmd/tiny, with the source as a file:// URL, with the target ../cmd/tiny, with the source https://example.com/service.git, and with a file:// URL that names a host.
then: Expects the first two to pass the checks of the flags and be refused only for the SDK that is not pinned; and each of the other three to be refused with the flag, the value found (for a URL, only its scheme and host) and what is expected; and no run to change the folder.
notes: Developer walkthrough of 2026-11-13, step 25 side notes: --target ./out was refused as 'requires a commit, relative module, and relative target', and --source file://... was read as a local path. checkLocation now names each flag; stego build takes the same checks. Mutations caught: no removal of ./ from the target; no file:// source.

title: A refused --source names only the scheme and the host of a URL, so no token is shown
when: stego build download and stego build run with --source set to https, ssh and file URLs that hold user info with a token, one with two @ signs, three with a raw /, ? or # in the user info, one with a token in the path, query and fragment, an scp-style user:TOKEN@host:path that is read as a local path, and two values whose scheme is not one of RFC 3986 and holds a token.
then: Expects each run to be refused with --source and only the scheme and the host of the URL, or only the scheme when the host is not certain, or the cause with no path for the local path; and no part of the user info, path, query or fragment in the refusal.
notes: Security review low S3 of #269, S3 of #273 and the low of #278 (CWE-532). Mutations caught: no @ guard when the parser finds no user info; the path kept; the raw path error in download and in build; the path error not unwrapped; the raw scheme shown.

title: A file:// source and a ./ module are cleaned to the same path as their plain forms
when: The location check runs on file:///a/../b with module ./m, file:///a/./b/ with module ./m/n, and /a//b/../c with module ., and on their plain clean forms.
then: Expects each pair to give the same source and module, and the source to be clean.
notes: Security review low S3 of #269. Mutation caught: no clean of the source.

title: The runtime folder that is STEGO's registry pin supplies it with no module proxy
when: With a committed module that imports a package of the runtime library at the version STEGO's registry pins, the runtime folder of STEGO's own repository in the source, go.sum with its hashes, and the pinned Go SDK: stego build download runs.
then: The download succeeds, and the cache holds exactly the zip of the runtime pin, whose hash is the pin that the binary carries.
notes: It needs the Go SDK that STEGO pins: STEGO_TEST_PINNED_GO names its bin/go, else the SDK that runs the test is used, and the test skips when STEGO refuses that SDK as not the pinned one. A skip is not a pass. It reaches the module proxy for the go.mod files of the runtime library's requirements, and sum.golang.org.

title: A runtime folder that differs from the pin stops the download, which names both hashes and leaves nothing
when: With the same source, but go.sum states a wrong hash for the runtime pin, and the pinned Go SDK: stego build download runs.
then: The download fails, names the module, its version, the hash go.sum states, the hash of the folder and the folder, and leaves nothing in the parent folder.

Then, against one stand-in: a kept tree that is garbage, larger than 64 KiB, a link or writable by others; a folder that others may write; a folder that is a link; and a run while another run holds the lock of the folder. Then opens a kept-tree folder, moves it, puts another folder at its path and writes a tree; and waits five times, 50 ms each, for the lock of a folder that another run holds. Then opens a kept tree under a parent folder that is a link to another folder of the user, and under a parent folder that others may write.
then: Each of the first is refused; the refusal names the module, its version and the hash expected, or the link, and no proxy folder is written. The last three are staged, since the binary's pin matches. Through the stand-in, the lookup gives the stated hash, gives not found with no error for the 404, and gives a lookup error that is not the inconsistency error for the bad signature; the folder is refused for the other hash and staged for the other three. The two runs against the first are staged and the kept tree is a file only its owner reads; the run against the fork is refused because its tiles do not prove a signed tree; the run with no kept tree is staged. Each bad kept tree is removed with a warning that names the file and the good tree is kept again; the unsafe folder and the linked folder are left out with a warning and hold no tree; the second run waits until the lock is released. The tree is in the folder that was opened and not at the path; each wait ends with its deadline, and no goroutine is left running. Both are refused, and nothing is made in the folder that the link names or in the open parent.
notes: The lookup step (lookupSumDBAt) takes the URL, the key and the HTTP client of the sum database, so the test reaches a local httptest stand-in of golang.org/x/mod/sumdb and never sum.golang.org (ST-STD-LOCAL). Added for the #214 delta recheck gap (follow-up worker, fu-2). Mutations caught: a 404 not read as not found; the hash the sum database states not compared; the default HTTP client in place of the server's. The lookup keeps no signed tree between runs, so it cannot meet a fork (errSumDBInconsistent) on one answer; the stand-ins of the earlier cases cover that refusal. The lookup now keeps the latest signed tree in stego/sumdb of the user cache, as the go command keeps it in GOPATH/pkg/sumdb, and tiles that do not prove a signed tree are the inconsistency error (#226 info item). Mutations caught: no kept tree; inconsistent tiles taken as a plain lookup error. Lows L1 to L3 of the security review of PR #235: the kept tree is read, compared and written under flock of its folder (lock), the folder and the file must be the current user's alone and no link, a bad kept tree is removed and kept again, and every lookup error is logged. Mutations caught: no removal of a bad tree; no check of the mode; no lock; no check of the signed note. The Lstat of the file is backed by O_NOFOLLOW, so its mutation alone is equivalent. #235 residual: every file of the folder is reached through one O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW handle (openat, renameat, unlinkat), and the lock wait polls with LOCK_NB, so nothing waits past its context. Mutations caught: the code before (written at the path, five goroutines left); a rename by path. #240 review L1: the folder is reached from the cache root through the parent and the folder, each with openat and O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW, made with mkdirat when missing and checked with fstat; no path below the cache root is followed. Mutations caught: the code before (a sumdb made in the folder that the parent links to); no O_NOFOLLOW in the walk; no check of the steps. #240 hardening: a cache root that is not the user's own folder that its group and others may not write, nor a folder of root with the sticky bit, leaves the kept tree out before anything is made in it; mutation caught: no check of the cache root. #259 info: a cache root that is a link must be the user's own link (Lstat before the open), because with fs.protected_symlinks=0 the kernel follows a link of another user in a shared folder; a cache root that is the user's own link is used. A test cannot make a link of another user, so it replaces the Lstat of the cache root (lstatRoot) to give the user's own link with another owner, and drives the refusal through openKeptTree. #264 review L1: a cache root that is no link at the Lstat is opened with O_NOFOLLOW, so a link that another user swaps in after the Lstat is refused; the test gives the Lstat of the folder that the link names. Mutations caught: no call of the check in the walk; no O_NOFOLLOW at the open of the cache root.

title: A create writes the relationship through the outbox after commit, and the stored instance holds the consistency token
when: The service generated from ST-DECL-TD03 runs. u1 creates a Todo with owner_id u1. The test reads the outbox in the same transaction view, the fake provider's calls after the relay runs, and the stored Todo.
then: Expects one outbox row for document:<id>#owner@user:u1 committed with the Todo. Expects the fake provider to get that write only from the relay, after commit, and the stored Todo to hold the consistency token the provider gave back.
notes: The test runs stego apply on the declaration of ST-DECL-TD03 in the form that the runtime data path generates, builds the service with the pinned Go SDK and drives it over HTTP, against PostgreSQL in a local container and the fakes of ST-DECL-TD05 (ST-STD-LOCAL). The fake authorization provider is a SpiceDB gRPC server in the process of the check; it holds the relationships that it gets and records each call. The host test is internal/compiler/relationship_outbox_test.go. On the runtime data path the create of the top-level Todo is public (ST-SUP-RC29-OC01), and a public create cannot write a field-sourced relationship (ST-SUP-Q118), so the owner relationship has the subject source caller. u1 sends owner_id u1. The check reads the Todo and the outbox in one snapshot, and the fake reads whether the row of the Todo is committed when the write comes.

title: Generation refuses a declaration that binds authorization while the registry holds no spicedb-authz, naming the component
when: With a copy of the registry of ST-DECL-TD01 without the component spicedb-authz: stego validate runs on ST-DECL-TD03, then stego plan, then stego apply.

notes: Proved by TestDeclareAuthorization, subtest ST-DECL-UC06-R07-T06. Authorization fails closed: STEGO never generates a service without the checks its declaration binds. The refusal is of the registry, not of the declaration, so it is not a declaration fault (ST-DECL-UC03-R03). The test runs the stego binary built from the commit under test in a temporary project folder of ST-DECL-TD03 (internal/declaration/testdata/td03), whose configuration names the copy of the registry without spicedb-authz, because the registry of ST-DECL-TD01 holds it since ST-SUP-RC29 (2026-11-10). Decision of 2026-11-09 under the owner's delegation, on question ST-DECL-Q08 and the review of PR 165. On the runtime data path the runtime wiring calls the component, so the check of generation that stego validate runs refuses the declaration too, with the same cause and no declaration fault. Decided by orchestrator under owner delegation, 2026-11-12 (single data path, RC20-OC39 PR 2).

title: Generation runs once the registry holds spicedb-authz, and the generated service builds
when: With the registry of ST-DECL-TD01, which holds spicedb-authz: stego validate runs on ST-DECL-TD03, then stego plan, then stego apply, and then go build of the applied service.
then: Expects stego validate to accept the declaration, stego plan to plan internal/authz/authz.go and internal/authz/schema.zed, stego apply to exit 0 with schema.zed the declared schema with one floor marker definition stego_floor, and the applied service to build.
notes: Proved by TestDeclareAuthorization, subtest ST-DECL-UC06-R07-T07. The refusal of ST-DECL-UC06-R07-T06 lifts once the registry holds the component that generates the authorization checks (ST-SUP-RC29). The spicedb-authz component needs pooled tenancy on tenant_id, because every resource ID at the provider is tenant-qualified (ST-SUP-RP06-LC22), and ST-DECL-TD03 declares it. The build runs against registry/runtime through the work file of scripts/runtime-workspace.sh, with the Go SDK of STEGO_TEST_PINNED_GO. The test runs the stego binary built from the commit under test in a temporary project folder of ST-DECL-TD03 (internal/declaration/testdata/td03). A stego build without the spicedb-authz generator, or a compiler that does not capture the schema, fails it.

title: The same key with another method is not a replay
when: ST-DECL-TD02 is changed to declare idempotency required on create and patch, with the default fingerprint. The service generated from it runs. u1 creates a Todo. Then u1 sends PATCH to that Todo's path with the key K4 and a body, then POST to the same path with the key K4 and the same body.
then: Expects the POST response not to be the stored response of the PATCH, byte for byte.
notes: Not automated yet: the generated code is not built. The test runs stego apply, builds the service with the pinned Go SDK and drives it over HTTP; it runs on the developer workstation against PostgreSQL in a local container and the fakes of ST-DECL-TD05 (ST-STD-LOCAL). Only the method differs between the two requests, so a fingerprint that leaves the method out fails; a POST to todos and a PATCH to one Todo differ in the path too, and would not show it. If the declaration format offers a custom operation served by POST on the Todo's path, the builder uses it for the POST, so that the request reaches the idempotency check and is not only refused by routing.

then: Expects the hash and the modification time of each file in the folder to be the same after each run as before it, and no file to be added.
notes: stego env check runs as a child process with --requirements and the environment file of the test data set.

title: An environment file that cannot be read is a failed check that names the file and the place
when: The environment file is changed so that it is not valid YAML at line 4. stego env check runs; then it runs on an environment file path that does not exist.
then: Expects each run to exit non-zero, naming the file, and for the first run line 4. Expects no output to say that the environment meets the requirements.
notes: stego env check runs as a child process with --requirements and the environment file of the test data set.

title: Platform requirements that cannot be read or have an unknown shape are a failed check that names the file and the place

notes: stego env check runs as a child process with --requirements and the environment file of the test data set.

title: An environment file of an unknown shape is a failed check that names the place

notes: stego env check runs as a child process with --requirements and the environment file of the test data set.

title: A value that no requirement names is listed as unused, and the check still passes

then: Expects it to exit 0, to report that the environment meets each requirement, and to list secret legacy-cache and configuration LOG_FORMAT as unused.
notes: stego env check runs as a child process with --requirements and the environment file of the test data set.

title: An unused value does not change why the check fails
when: The environment file gets the configuration value LOG_FORMAT, which no requirement names, and loses the egress payments. stego env check runs.
then: Expects it to exit non-zero, naming the egress payments as the one unmet requirement, and to list LOG_FORMAT as unused, not as a cause of the failure.
notes: stego env check runs as a child process with --requirements and the environment file of the test data set.

title: The hosted CI pipeline runs each of the five STEGO checks before it releases the image

notes: Runs on the developer workstation against the local stand-in of the hosted CI provider of ST-DLV-TD04 (ST-STD-LOCAL). A run on the real provider MAY follow as a second proof.

title: The Konflux pipeline runs each of the five STEGO checks before it releases the image

then: Expects the pipeline run to have a STEGO checks task whose results show drift, vet, test, the reproducible build and the executable match each as passed, and the image to be released only after that task passes.
notes: Runs on the developer workstation against the local Konflux stand-in of ST-DLV-TD05 (Tekton Pipelines and Tekton Chains in a local kind cluster that run the pinned Konflux standard pipeline bundle) (ST-STD-LOCAL). A run on a real Konflux tenant MAY follow as a second proof.

title: On the hosted CI provider, a failure of any one STEGO check releases no image

then: Expects each run to fail at the check that the change breaks, naming that check, and to publish no image to the test image repository.
notes: Runs on the developer workstation against the local stand-in of the hosted CI provider of ST-DLV-TD04 (ST-STD-LOCAL). A run on the real provider MAY follow as a second proof. Five changes, one per check, so that a check that a pipeline leaves out is caught.

title: On Konflux, a failure of any one STEGO check releases no image
when: Five pushes start the generated PipelineRun on Konflux, each with one change that makes one check fail: drift (a generated file edited by hand), vet (a vet finding in a fill), test (a fill test that fails), the reproducible build (an input that makes the second build differ), and the executable match (an image whose executable differs from the record).
then: Expects each pipeline run to fail at the STEGO checks task, naming the check that the change breaks, and no image of the run to be released for delivery.
notes: Runs on the developer workstation against the local Konflux stand-in of ST-DLV-TD05 (Tekton Pipelines and Tekton Chains in a local kind cluster that run the pinned Konflux standard pipeline bundle) (ST-STD-LOCAL). A run on a real Konflux tenant MAY follow as a second proof.

notes: stego delivery check runs as a child process with --image, --record and --record-sha256.

A run on a real Konflux tenant MAY follow as a second proof. ST-DLV-INV07-T proves the same Containerfile with buildah alone.

title: On Konflux, a prefetched module that does not match the module checksums stops the build

notes: Runs on the developer workstation against the local Konflux stand-in of ST-DLV-TD05 (Tekton Pipelines and Tekton Chains in a local kind cluster that run the pinned Konflux standard pipeline bundle) (ST-STD-LOCAL). A run on a real Konflux tenant MAY follow as a second proof.

title: A hosted CI image is signed by the keyless identity of the pinned shared pipeline, and by no other

A run on the real provider MAY follow as a second proof.

title: A Konflux image is signed by the Tekton Chains key

notes: Runs on the developer workstation against the local Konflux stand-in of ST-DLV-TD05 (Tekton Pipelines and Tekton Chains in a local kind cluster that run the pinned Konflux standard pipeline bundle) (ST-STD-LOCAL). A run on a real Konflux tenant MAY follow as a second proof.

title: The delivery check refuses an image signed by a signer that is not its provider's trusted signer
when: stego delivery check runs on a copy of the hosted image of the test data set signed with the test Tekton Chains key, and on a copy signed with a key the registry does not name.
then: Expects each run to exit non-zero, naming the signer found and the trusted signer of the provider that built the image.
notes: An image that carries a signer of the other provider is the case that catches a check that accepts any trusted signer, not the one of its provider.

title: The delivery check passes an image that also carries another signature, and refuses one whose only valid signature is another signer's
when: Make two copies of the hosted image of the test data set, which the trusted signer of the hosted CI provider signed. Add to the first copy a second signature by a test key K3 that the registry does not name, as a mirror or a promotion adds one. On the second copy, replace the trusted signer's signature with one over another digest, so that it does not verify, and add a valid signature by K3. Run stego delivery check on each copy.
then: Expects the run on the first copy to exit 0, with the signature check passed and naming the trusted signer. Expects the run on the second copy to exit non-zero, naming the trusted signer of the hosted CI provider as the signer with no valid signature, and not reporting the image as signed.
notes: Decision on review item R1 of the Delivering test plan, reading b: only the trusted signer's signature counts. The first copy catches a check that refuses an image with any other signature. The second copy catches a check that passes an image when any one of its signatures verifies.

title: Applying the plan writes the delivery policy file from the declaration and the registry's advisories
when: stego apply runs on the service of the test data set; then the registry copy gets an advisory that withdraws the digest of one component that the declaration uses, and stego apply runs again.
then: Expects the first run to write the delivery policy file at the path that the CI file passes to the pipeline, with the trusted signer and the image targets of the declaration. Expects the second run to change the policy file so that it refuses the withdrawn digest, naming the advisory.
notes: The stego binary runs as a child process from a test in cmd/stego, with the project folder of the test data set as its working folder.

title: The delivery check evaluates the policy file that the pipeline carries
when: stego apply runs on a copy of the service of the test data set with a registry copy whose ci-pipeline component names the test key K2 as the trusted signer of the hosted CI provider, and its delivery policy file is kept. With the original registry, and the hosted image signed by the trusted signer of that registry: stego delivery check runs on the image with --policy and --policy-sha256 naming the delivery policy file that stego apply wrote from the original registry and its digest; then again with --policy and --policy-sha256 naming the kept policy file and its digest.
then: Expects the first run to pass and to name the policy file it evaluated. Expects the second run to exit non-zero, naming the signer found in the image, K2 as the trusted signer that the policy names, and the kept policy file.
notes: The registry does not change between the two runs, so a check that derives its own policy from the registry, and not from the file that the pipeline carries, gives the same result twice and fails the test. Decision on review item R2 of the Delivering test plan: the check takes --policy and --policy-sha256, as it takes the build record (ST-DLV-CLI01). Decision on ST-DLV-Q02: the platform's gate is the platform's to prove, so this test proves STEGO's half only.

title: The delivery check refuses a policy file whose digest is not the trusted digest, before any check, and the CI file passes the policy file and its digest
when: stego apply runs on the service of the test data set. Read the delivery check step of the hosted CI file and of the Konflux PipelineRun. Then change one byte of the delivery policy file that apply wrote, and run stego delivery check on the hosted image with --policy naming that file and --policy-sha256 the digest of the file before the change.
then: Expects the delivery check step of each CI file to pass --policy with the path of the policy file that apply wrote and --policy-sha256 with that file's SHA-256 digest. Expects the run to exit non-zero, naming the policy file and the two digests, and to print no result of any image check.
notes: Decision on review item R2 of the Delivering test plan, reading a. A check that reads the policy file and does not compare its digest passes the changed file and fails the test. That no image check runs catches a check that compares the digest after it evaluates the policy.

title: Applying the plan takes each pin and the trusted signer of the CI file from the registry's ci-pipeline component
when: stego apply runs on the service of the test data set; then on a copy whose delivery stanza names Konflux.
then: Expects each pinned reference and the trusted signer in the hosted CI file and in the Konflux PipelineRun to equal what the ci-pipeline component names.
notes: The stego binary runs as a child process from a test in cmd/stego, with the project folder of the test data set as its working folder.

title: A declaration that sets a trusted signer is refused, naming the path

then: Expects stego apply to exit non-zero, naming the path of the field in the declaration as not declared, and no file of the project folder to change.

title: A ci-pipeline version that changes one pin changes only that pin in each service's CI file

notes: The stego binary runs as a child process from a test in cmd/stego, with the project folder of the test data set as its working folder.

title: A ci-pipeline component whose reference uses a tag, a branch or a short hash is refused
when: Three runs of stego apply on the service of the test data set, each with a registry copy whose ci-pipeline component pins the shared pipeline by the tag v1.2.0, by the branch main, or by the short hash 0123456.
then: Expects each run to exit non-zero, naming the ci-pipeline component and the reference, and no file of the project folder to change.
notes: The stego binary runs as a child process from a test in cmd/stego, with the project folder of the test data set as its working folder.

notes: The command's statement is the one of ST-GEN-UC03-R03; ST-GEN-CLI01 says today that stego apply takes no flag, which the Generating domain must change. The stego binary runs as a child process from a test in cmd/stego, with the project folder of the test data set as its working folder.

when: stego apply runs on the service of the test data set.
then: Expects the CI file to hold one job, which calls the platform's shared pipeline at the 40-character commit that the registry names and passes the STEGO checks reference by its pin, with no step or script of its own and no other job.
notes: The stego binary runs as a child process from a test in cmd/stego, with the project folder of the test data set as its working folder.

title: For Konflux, applying the plan writes a PipelineRun that only references the standard pipeline bundle and the STEGO checks by digest

notes: The stego binary runs as a child process from a test in cmd/stego, with the project folder of the test data set as its working folder.

title: The written Kubernetes base sets no replicas, PodDisruptionBudget, namespace, image digest, host name, egress address or secret value

The requirement forbids an image digest; it does not forbid an image name or tag, so the test does not refuse one. The stego binary runs as a child process from a test in cmd/stego, with the project folder of the test data set as its working folder.

title: The written Kubernetes base carries the probes that health-check derives

then: Expects each command to exit non-zero with a fault that names qualified-fill, the slot rest-api.before_create, the bound collection org-groups and the fill's collection org-users. Expects apply to leave the out folder and the record byte for byte as they were.
notes: ListQualification (ST-EXT-QRY02-H) and its use by plan and apply are not built. The fill is qualified, so only the misfit can cause the refusal.

title: stego test records no evidence for a fill that imports a module the declaration does not list, and names the import

title: stego test records no evidence for a fill that imports a module whose path only starts with a listed module's path

then: Expects the output to name untested-fill and github.com/google/uuidx, and fill.yaml of untested-fill to stay byte for byte as it was.
notes: Resolve github.com/google/uuidx through a replace directive to a fixture module. This catches a check that compares import paths by string prefix.

title: stego test records no evidence for a fill that imports a generated package other than out/slots, and names the import

The imports of test files are ST-EXT-UC01-R03-T04 and T05.

notes: A test file is a file whose name ends in _test.go; it is not built into the service, so the import rule does not hold for it (decision on ST-EXT-Q01). This catches a check that reads every Go file of the fill folder. Resolve testify through a replace directive to a fixture module, so that the test runs with the network off.

title: stego test records no evidence for a fill whose built file imports a test module, even when the file name holds the word test

then: Expects the output to name untested-fill, testutil.go and github.com/stretchr/testify/assert, and fill.yaml of untested-fill to stay byte for byte as it was.

notes: Owner decision of 2026-11-06: every fill, at every slot, is held to one fill allow list of the standard library, checked over everything it imports. notes: Owner decision of 2026-11-06: every fill, at every slot, is held to one fill allow list of the standard library, checked over everything it imports. Resolve the fixture modules through replace directives to folders of the project, so the test runs with the network off. The example fills of examples/user-management and examples/user-management-rhsso dropped net/http for literal status codes when this rule was built, and a person must sign them again. The test makes one copy of untested-fill for each package and runs stego test once; each copy has one change, so each refusal stands alone.

title: stego test records evidence for a fill that imports only allow-listed packages, whose own closure holds os

Resolve the fixture modules through replace directives to folders of the project, so the test runs with the network off. The example fills of examples/user-management and examples/user-management-rhsso dropped net/http for literal status codes when this rule was built, and a person must sign them again.

title: stego test records no evidence for a fill that holds code its imports do not show
when: Make copies of untested-fill, each with one change: an assembly file write_amd64.s with a function declared with no body in policy.go; an assembly file of another platform; a .syso file; a C file in a folder under the fill; a //go:linkname directive on a function with no body; a //go:cgo_import_dynamic directive; a //go:embed directive; a file that imports C; an import of the fill's own package _sub, which holds an assembly file and a function with no body. Run stego test.
then: Expects each copy to get no evidence, with fill.yaml byte for byte as it was, and the output to name the copy and the file that is not Go source, the function with no body, the directive, the import of C, or the import of _sub with its assembly file and its function with no body.
notes: The baseline security review of 2026-11-11 (finding 2) showed that a fill with an assembly file makes a raw system call with no import at all, so the import rule alone does not hold. A fill folder holds only Go source files, its fill.yaml and test data under testdata. The directives and the functions with no body are the other ways to reach code that no import shows. The security review of PR 207 showed that a package of the fill under a folder that starts with _ or . or is testdata builds when the fill imports it by its path; such an import is refused, and the files of that package are named. The file that imports C is left out of the service build, which has no cgo, so the fault names it from the fill folder. See the decision on ST-EXT-Q05 (2026-11-11).

It runs the stego binary and the service binaries built from the commits of ST-GEN-TD04 (v1 and v2 with the add and the rename at expand, the interim scope of the harness) against the runtime module of the commit under test, on PostgreSQL 17.7 given as STEGO_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN and authzed/spicedb v1.57.0 in local unprivileged containers with 512 MiB and 1 CPU (ST-STD-LOCAL); it is not a stress test.
