title: A declared fill value repairs the rows that failed the conversion
when: From a copy of ST-GEN-TD04 whose v1 has the field OrgSetting.revision (string, pattern ^[0-9]+$) and whose v2 retypes it to integer with text_to_integer and integer_to_text: the test writes 3 rows with SQL as the owner role whose revision breaks the pattern; v2's backfill runs to completion; the migration job of v3 runs; then a v2.1 declares the fill value 0, stego compat --base v2 runs, v2.1 is deployed, its backfill runs, and the migration job of v3 runs again.
then: Expects the first backfill to report 3 failed rows, the first contract to fail with the change and the count 3, stego compat to accept the added fill value, the second backfill to give the 3 rows the value 0, and the second contract to succeed.
notes: Not automated yet: the backfill is not built. The test runs the service binaries of ST-GEN-TD04 on PostgreSQL in an unprivileged rootless container with CPU and memory limits, with a lease TTL of 2 s and a batch size of 500 so that it runs in seconds; it is not a stress test. Planned file cmd/stego/schema_backfill_test.go.

title: A base declaration that is not the one its record names is refused
when: From ST-GEN-TD03: a second commit changes the title field's max_length in service.yaml and does not run apply, so the record names the digest of the first service.yaml; stego compat --base HEAD runs on the same service.yaml.
then: Expects exit 1 and a fault that names the base ref, its commit, the digest in the record and the digest of the base declaration.
notes: The test runs the stego binary built from the commit under test, in a temporary folder with no network.

title: With no record at the base ref, any stored shape is accepted
when: In a new git repository whose one commit holds the service.yaml of ST-GEN-TD03 and no record: the head renames Note.title to heading and adds a required field owner with no default, with no schema change, and stego compat --base HEAD runs.
then: Expects exit 0 and no fault.
notes: The test runs the stego binary built from the commit under test, in a temporary folder with no network.

title: Each fault names the entity, the field, the rule and the schema change and phase to declare
when: From ST-GEN-TD03, whose one commit is the base: stego compat --base HEAD --json runs on five heads with no schema change: Note.title renamed to heading; Note.title retyped to integer; a new required field Note.owner with no default; a new declared invariant unique on Note by title; Note.title removed and a field body added.
then: Expects exit 1 for each head and one fault for each. Each fault names Note, the field, the rule ST-GEN-INV33, and the schema change to declare: rename from title at expand, retype from string at expand with a conversion, require with a fill value at expand, unique at expand, and drop at expand with add for body.
notes: The test runs the stego binary built from the commit under test, in a temporary folder with no network.

title: The check names the base ref and its commit with and without a fault
when: From ST-GEN-TD03: stego compat --base HEAD runs on the unchanged declaration, then on a declaration with an undeclared rename of Note.title, then with --json.
then: Expects each output to name HEAD and the full commit of HEAD, and the JSON object to hold them as the base ref and the base commit.
notes: The test runs the stego binary built from the commit under test, in a temporary folder with no network.

title: The documentation of the check names the base ref as the running version and a skipped release as the operator's risk
when: A documentation test reads the page for stego compat and the page for schema changes under docs/.
then: Expects each page to state that the check takes the declaration at the base ref as the version that runs now, and that a release which is not deployed before the next one is the operator's risk.
notes: The test reads docs/compat.md and docs/schema-changes.md as text and needs no stego binary. STEGO's own spec holds no manual test (ST-ASR-Q01).

title: The contract migration refuses while rows are left and writes no ledger row
when: From ST-GEN-TD04 after the migration job of v2 and a backfill stopped at 3,000 rows: the migration job of v3 runs; then the backfill completes, a test session sets contact_email of one row to NULL with the trigger disabled, and the job runs again.
then: Expects both runs to exit non-zero, to name user-email-rename and the count of rows left (7,000, then 1), to write no ledger row, and to leave the catalog of the users table as it was.
notes: Not automated yet: schema steps are not built. The test runs the stego binary and the service binaries built from the commits of ST-GEN-TD04, on PostgreSQL in an unprivileged rootless container with CPU and memory limits; it is not a stress test. Planned file cmd/stego/schema_evolution_test.go.

title: After contract the old column and the trigger are gone and the contract release does not need them
when: From ST-GEN-TD04 with the backfill complete: the migration job of v3 runs, a v3 api replica starts, and a client creates, reads, changes and lists users through it.
then: Expects the users table to have no email column and no trigger, contact_email NOT NULL with its unique index, and each request through v3 to succeed.
notes: Not automated yet: schema steps are not built. The test runs the stego binary and the service binaries built from the commits of ST-GEN-TD04, on PostgreSQL in an unprivileged rootless container with CPU and memory limits; it is not a stress test. Planned file cmd/stego/schema_evolution_test.go.

title: A finished change can go only by a new baseline, which the upgraded database accepts
when: From ST-GEN-TD04 with v3 migrated: the author removes user-email-rename and its steps and runs stego compat --base v3; then runs stego fix with a registry that accepts the next declaration version, stego compat --base v3, stego apply, and starts the new binary on the database and on a new database.
then: Expects the first compat to exit 1 and name user-email-rename. Expects fix to fold the finished change into a new baseline, the second compat to exit 0, and the new binary to start on both databases with no migration run on the upgraded one and the same catalog on both.
notes: Not automated yet: schema steps are not built. The test runs the stego binary and the service binaries built from the commits of ST-GEN-TD04, on PostgreSQL in an unprivileged rootless container with CPU and memory limits; it is not a stress test. Planned file cmd/stego/schema_evolution_test.go. The registry copy accepts the next declaration version as in ST-GEN-UC10-R01-T01.

title: A component with no config schema is refused, and its generator does not run
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, run stego registry add on the folder of a new component new-a that has ports, slots and a namespace but no config schema, and whose generator writes a marker file when it runs.
then: Expects a non-zero exit, a message that names new-a and the config schema as missing, no marker file, and the registry checkout unchanged.

title: A component whose generator reads a setting, a port or a slot that it does not declare is refused before any file is written
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, run stego registry add three times on new-a, whose generator writes a marker file when it runs: once where its generator reads the setting retries, which the config schema does not hold; once where it reads the port cache-port, which the component does not require; and once where it invokes the slot after_save, which the component does not offer.
then: Expects each add to exit non-zero, naming new-a and the undeclared setting, port or slot, with no marker file and the registry checkout unchanged.
notes: Whether STEGO finds the undeclared input by a static scan of the generator or by giving the generator only its declared inputs is the builder's choice; the test asserts the refusal before a file is written.

title: A component that declares its config schema, its ports and its slots is accepted
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, run stego registry add on the full folder of new-a, whose generator writes a marker file when it runs.
then: Expects exit 0 and output that names new-a and its version as accepted.
notes: The add may run the generator after the declared inputs are checked, because ST-SUP-UC01-R06 needs two renders on add; ST-SUP-UC01-R01-T01 proves that the generator does not run before the check.

title: A component whose namespace another component claims is refused, naming both
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, run stego registry add on new-b with the namespace internal/store, which store-a claims; then with Internal/Store; then with internal/store/cache, which is inside it.
then: Expects each run to exit non-zero and name new-b, store-a and both namespaces, with the registry unchanged.
notes: The case of the letters and a path inside the claimed one are each a claim, as the namespace check of the compiler holds today.

title: A namespace that only starts with the same letters as a claimed one is accepted
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, run stego registry add on new-b with the namespace internal/storefront.
then: Expects exit 0 and new-b accepted.
notes: This catches a check by string prefix that refuses internal/storefront because of internal/store.

title: Two components in two sources that claim one namespace are refused, naming both
when: With ST-SUP-TD02, give local-a the namespace internal/store, which store-a of the common registry claims, and run stego registry compose.
then: Expects a non-zero exit and a message that names local-a, store-a, the namespace and both registries.

title: A release whose emitted code changed under the old version is refused
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, change one template of store-a so that its emitted code changes, and run stego registry release store-a --version 1.0.0.
then: Expects a non-zero exit, and a message that names store-a, version 1.0.0 and a file whose emitted code changed. Expects no version to be recorded.

title: A component whose emitted code changed without a new version is refused
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, change one template of store-a so that its emitted code changes, keep its version 1.0.0, and run stego registry compose and stego plan.
then: Expects both to exit non-zero, naming store-a and version 1.0.0 as released with other emitted code.
notes: The registry must keep, for each released version, a digest of what it emits, to compare with. Where it is kept is the builder's choice.

title: A release at a new version records the version
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, change one template of store-a and run stego registry release store-a --version 1.1.0; then run stego registry inspect store-a.
then: Expects exit 0 and output that names 1.1.0; expects inspect to show version 1.1.0.

title: Every output contract of a component names the code that builds it and the test that proves it
when: Runs lathe check on STEGO's specification, and on a fixture specification with one component whose output contracts are: one with its generator and its test, one with no generator, and one with no test.
then: Expects no output contract of a shipped component to be reported as not built or not proved for want of a generator or a test. Expects the fixture's second contract to be reported as not built and its third as not proved, each by its ID.
notes: This proves only that each contract names its code and its test. Decision on ST-SUP-Q06, as revised by the coordinator on 2026-11-04: completeness is a review duty of the platform engineer at release, whose check is the reference comparison that ST-SUP-SP07-T proves, and no mechanical check counts the MUSTs of a contract; STEGO's spec holds no manual test (ST-ASR-Q01), so the review itself has no test record. On today's spec, 126 output contracts of Supplying are not proved, so this test fails until they are.

title: A component that states no architecture role is refused, naming the component
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, run stego registry add on new-a with no architecture role.
then: Expects a non-zero exit and a message that names new-a and the architecture role, with the registry unchanged.

title: A component whose role leaves out its layer, its part in a request flow or the side of one port is refused, naming the part
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, run stego registry add three times on new-a, which provides new-port and requires store-port: without its layer, without its part in a request flow, and with a side for new-port and none for store-port.
then: Expects each run to exit non-zero and name new-a and the missing part: the layer, the part in a request flow, or store-port.

title: Adding a component that emits a static file is refused, naming each static file
when: With ST-SUP-TD01 and ST-SUP-TD04, run stego registry add on static-gen, which emits two static files, internal/static/util.go and internal/static/mod.go, and one file that varies.
then: Expects a non-zero exit and a message that names static-gen, both static files and the runtime library as where they belong, and not the file that varies.

title: Releasing a version that adds a static file is refused, naming the file
when: With ST-SUP-TD01 and ST-SUP-TD04, add to store-a a template that emits internal/store/version.go with fixed text, and run stego registry release store-a --version 1.1.0.
then: Expects a non-zero exit, a message that names store-a and internal/store/version.go, and no version 1.1.0 recorded.

title: Adding a component whose schema marks a setting or a slot input as a bypass is refused, naming each marked one
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, run stego registry add on bypass-a, whose config schema declares the settings skip_authz, marked as a bypass, and cache_ttl, not marked, and whose slot before_check declares the input skip_check, marked as a bypass. Then run stego registry add on plain-a, which is bypass-a with both marks removed.
then: Expects the first add to exit non-zero with a message that names bypass-a, skip_authz and skip_check, and not cache_ttl, and the registry to hold no bypass-a. Expects the second add to exit 0.
notes: Not automated yet: no check reads a bypass mark. Decision of the Product owner on review item 7 of the Declaring test plan. Two marks in two places catch a check that stops at the first, or that reads the config schema only. plain-a catches a check by the names of the settings.

title: Releasing a version of a component that adds a bypass mark is refused, naming the marked setting
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, mark the setting of store-a's config schema as a bypass, and release store-a at version 1.1.0.
then: Expects a non-zero exit and a message that names store-a, 1.1.0 and the marked setting, and the registry to keep store-a at 1.0.0 at its old digest.
notes: Not automated yet: no check reads a bypass mark. A check that runs on add only fails the test.

title: A local component with the name of a common component is refused, naming the part and both registries
when: With ST-SUP-TD02, add to the local registry a component named store-a, once byte-identical to the common store-a and once changed, and run stego registry compose each time.
then: Expects both runs to exit non-zero and name store-a, the common registry and the local registry by their locations and commits.

title: A local archetype, mixin or port with the name of a common one is refused, naming the part and both registries
when: With ST-SUP-TD02, add to the local registry, one at a time, the archetype svc-arch, the mixin extra-mixin and the port store-port, and run stego registry compose each time.
then: Expects each run to exit non-zero and name the part, its kind and both registries.

title: The record of a generated service names each registry source with its full commit
when: With ST-SUP-TD02, run stego apply for the example declaration and read the generation record.
then: Expects the record to list both sources in the configured order, each with its location, its subfolder when it has one, and its full commit SHA, and the content digest of the active registry.

title: Compose prints each source with its reference and the parts it adds
when: With ST-SUP-TD02, run stego registry compose.
then: Expects exit 0 and output that names the common registry with its commit and its parts, and the local registry with its commit and local-a.

title: A composition of nine sources is refused, and one of eight is accepted
when: With ST-SUP-TD02, add local registries until .stego/config.yaml names eight sources, and run stego registry compose; then add a ninth and run it again.
then: Expects the run with eight sources to exit 0, and the run with nine to exit non-zero and name the count and the limit of eight.

title: Two sources that supply one artifact name are refused, even as identical copies
when: With ST-SUP-TD02, add a second local registry that holds local-a, once byte-identical to the first local registry's local-a and once changed, and run stego registry compose each time.
then: Expects both runs to exit non-zero and name local-a and both local registries.
notes: Two local registries can clash with each other as well as with the common registry; this case has no common part in it.

title: Two sources that supply one input path are refused
when: With ST-SUP-TD02, add to the local registry the file common/types.proto, which the common registry also holds, and run stego registry compose.
then: Expects a non-zero exit and a message that names common/types.proto and both registries.

title: A symbolic link in a registry or a vendor path is refused
when: With ST-SUP-TD02, add a symbolic link inside the local registry's components folder and run stego registry compose; then remove it, vendor the local registry, make the vendor path a symbolic link to the copy, and run it again.
then: Expects both runs to exit non-zero, each naming the path of the symbolic link.

title: Combined inputs over 64 MiB are refused, and inputs at the limit are accepted
when: With ST-SUP-TD02, add files to the two sources so that each holds less than 64 MiB and together they hold 64 MiB and 1 byte, and run stego registry compose; then remove the extra byte and run it again.
then: Expects the first run to exit non-zero and name the 64 MiB limit, and the second run to exit 0.
notes: Each source is under the limit alone, so a check per source fails the test. The files are plain data files, made at run time and not committed, that no other check of the registry refuses.

title: Combined inputs over 4,096 files are refused, and 4,096 files are accepted
when: With ST-SUP-TD02, add small files to the two sources so that together they hold 4,097 files, and run stego registry compose; then remove one file and run it again.
then: Expects the first run to exit non-zero and name the limit of 4,096 files, and the second run to exit 0.
notes: The files are spread over both sources, so a count per source fails the test. They are plain data files, made at run time and not committed, that no other check of the registry refuses.

title: Every source is captured before any source is validated
when: With ST-SUP-TD02, make the component file of store-a in the first source invalid YAML, add a symbolic link to the second source, and run stego registry compose; then remove the symbolic link and run it again.
then: Expects the first run to exit non-zero and name the symbolic link in the second source, and not the invalid file in the first. Expects the second run to exit non-zero and name the invalid file of store-a.
notes: A capture fault of a later source comes before a validation fault of an earlier one, so a run that validates each source as it captures it fails the test.

title: A source pinned by a short, an upper-case or a branch reference is refused
when: With ST-SUP-TD02, pin the local registry by the first 12 characters of its commit SHA, then by its full SHA in capital letters, then by main, and run stego registry compose each time.
then: Expects each run to exit non-zero and name the local registry and its reference as not a full lower-case commit SHA, with no fetch made.

title: A cached copy is used only at the pinned commit
when: With ST-SUP-TD02, compose once so that STEGO caches the local registry; then move the HEAD of the cached copy to another commit, turn the network off, and run stego registry compose again.
then: Expects the second run either to read exactly the tree of the pinned commit, so that the content digest equals that of the first run, or to exit non-zero and name the local registry and its pin; never to read the tree of the other commit.

title: A vendored copy at another commit is refused without a fetch
when: With ST-SUP-TD02, vendor the local registry at a commit other than the pin, set its vendor path, and run stego registry compose with Git tracing on.
then: Expects a non-zero exit, a message that names the local registry, the pinned commit and the commit of the copy, and no fetch in the Git trace.

title: A vendored copy without version-control metadata is refused
when: With ST-SUP-TD02, vendor the local registry at the pin, remove its .git folder, and run stego registry compose.
then: Expects a non-zero exit and a message that names the vendor path as lacking version-control metadata.

title: A vendored copy with a modified, an ignored or an untracked file is refused
when: With ST-SUP-TD02, vendor the local registry at the pin, and run stego registry compose three times: with one tracked file changed, with one ignored file added, and with one untracked file added.
then: Expects each run to exit non-zero and name the vendor path and the file.
notes: An ignored file is a separate case, because git status without --ignored does not show it.

title: With a vendor path set, STEGO reads only the vendored copy and does not fetch
when: With ST-SUP-TD02, vendor the local registry at the pin, set its vendor path, set its location to an address that cannot be reached, and run stego registry compose with Git tracing on.
then: Expects exit 0, the parts of the vendored copy in the active set, and no fetch or clone in the Git trace.

title: A registry address that starts with a hyphen is refused before git runs
when: With a project whose registry source has the address --upload-pack=touch <marker> and a full commit SHA: resolve the registry.
then: Expects a refusal that names the address, no marker file, and no registry cache.
notes: Finding 7 of the baseline security review of 2026-11-11. The clone also passes the address after --, so git never reads it as an option.

title: A namespace entry for a component outside the active set is refused
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, give the example declaration a component_namespaces entry for local-only, which is not in its active component set, and run stego validate.
then: Expects a non-zero exit and a message that names local-only as outside the active set.

title: An empty or compiler-owned namespace path is refused
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, give the example declaration a component_namespaces entry for store-a with the empty path, then with contracts, then with contracts/store, and run stego validate each time.
then: Expects each run to exit non-zero and name store-a and the path, the second and third as owned by the compiler.

title: A nonempty per-component pin is refused before any source is resolved
when: With ST-SUP-TD02, add to .stego/config.yaml the entry pins with store-a: 1.0.0, set the local registry's location to an address that cannot be reached, and run stego registry compose with Git tracing on.
then: Expects a non-zero exit, a message that names the pins entry and store-a, and no Git command in the trace.

title: An environment override of the registry sources is warned of, and no warning is given without it
when: With ST-SUP-TD02, set STEGO_REGISTRY to a folder that holds a copy of the common registry, and run stego registry compose; then unset STEGO_REGISTRY and run it again.
then: Expects the first run to give a warning on standard error that names the folder of STEGO_REGISTRY and says that the configured sources are not used. Expects the second run to give no such warning.

title: An archetype with a required port that no component provides is refused, naming the port and the components that require it
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, remove auth-a from the archetype folder of svc-arch and run stego registry curate on it.
then: Expects a non-zero exit and a message that names auth-port and api-a, which requires it.

title: An archetype with two providers of a required port is refused, naming the port and both providers
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, add store-b, a second ga provider of store-port, to svc-arch with no default provider for store-port, and run stego registry curate.
then: Expects a non-zero exit and a message that names store-port, store-a, store-b and api-a.

title: An archetype that includes components below ga is refused, naming each with its stage
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, add beta-x (beta) and alpha-y (alpha) to svc-arch, and run stego registry curate.
then: Expects a non-zero exit and a message that names beta-x with beta and alpha-y with alpha.
notes: Two components below ga, so a check that stops at the first fails the test.

title: A mixin that brings a component below ga is refused, naming the component and its stage
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, run stego registry extend svc-arch --mixin on a mixin folder that adds beta-x (beta).
then: Expects a non-zero exit, a message that names the mixin, beta-x and beta, and svc-arch unchanged.

title: A fresh declaration of each shipped archetype passes checking
when: For each archetype of the shipped registry, run stego init with it in an empty folder, then stego validate.
then: Expects stego validate to exit 0 for each archetype.
notes: ST-DECL-UC01-R04 proves that the scaffold writes the smallest content; this test proves that the archetype supplies content that passes.

title: An archetype without example content, or with example content that checking refuses, is refused
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, run stego registry curate on svc-arch with no example content, then with example content that names an entity field of an unknown type.
then: Expects each run to exit non-zero and name svc-arch and its example content, the second with the fault that checking gives.

title: Each part of the example content is needed for checking to pass
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, take the example content of svc-arch, and for each top-level key and each list item in it, write a declaration without that one part and run stego validate.
then: Expects stego validate to exit non-zero for each one, so that no part can be removed and the content still pass.
notes: This proves that the content is the smallest. A key that checking does not need fails the test.

title: An alpha or beta component with no sunset date is refused
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, write the folder of exp-a with the stage beta and no sunset date, and load the registry with stego registry compose; then do the same with the stage alpha.
then: Expects each run to exit non-zero and name exp-a and its sunset date as missing.

title: A sunset date that is already past is refused, and a later date is accepted
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, run stego registry introduce on the folder of exp-a with --stage alpha --sunset set to yesterday; then with --sunset set to tomorrow.
then: Expects the first run to exit non-zero and name the date as past, with exp-a not added. Expects the second run to exit 0 and print exp-a with its stage and sunset.
notes: The dates are relative to the day the test runs.

title: A declaration that uses a beta component without accepting it by name is refused
when: With ST-SUP-TD02, write a declaration that uses local-a (beta) and accepts only another component, beta-y, by name; run stego validate.
then: Expects a non-zero exit and a message that names local-a and its stage, and says that the declaration does not accept it.
notes: The acceptance of another component is in the declaration, so a check that reads only whether an acceptance exists fails the test.

title: A declaration that accepts a beta component by name may use it
when: With ST-SUP-TD02, write a declaration that uses local-a and accepts local-a by name, with a reason and a date before its sunset; run stego validate.
then: Expects exit 0.

title: An experimental component with no outcome is refused, naming the outcome as missing
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, run stego registry introduce on exp-a with its references and its promise list but no outcome.
then: Expects a non-zero exit, a message that names exp-a and the outcome, and exp-a not added.

title: An experimental component with no reference and no reason why none exists is refused
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, run stego registry introduce on exp-a with its outcome and its promise list, and neither a reference nor a reason why none exists. Then run it with no reference and the reason.
then: Expects the first run to exit non-zero and name the references as missing, and the second run to exit 0.

title: An experimental component with no output contract is refused
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, run stego registry introduce on exp-a with its outcome and its references and an empty promise list.
then: Expects a non-zero exit and a message that names exp-a and its promise list as missing.

title: A reference promise that the promise list does not mention is refused, naming the promise
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, give exp-a the reference ref-1 with the promises p1, p2 and p3: p1 adopted as an output contract, p2 declined with a reason, and p3 not mentioned. Run stego registry introduce; then mention p3 as declined with a reason and run it again.
then: Expects the first run to exit non-zero and name ref-1 and p3, and not p1 or p2. Expects the second run to exit 0.

title: A declined promise without a reason is refused
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, give exp-a the promise p2 of ref-1 as declined with an empty reason, and run stego registry introduce.
then: Expects a non-zero exit and a message that names p2 and its reason as missing.

title: An experimental component is introduced before its generator is written
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, run stego registry introduce on a folder of exp-a with its outcome, references and promise list and no generator.
then: Expects exit 0 and exp-a added at alpha, so the request comes before the code.

title: stego registry consumers names every recorded service that uses a component, and no other
when: With ST-SUP-TD03, run stego registry consumers beta-x with the four checkouts.
then: Expects exit 0 and output that names svc-one with 0.2.0 and svc-two with 0.3.0, and not svc-three or svc-four. Expects no file of any checkout to change.

title: A ga component that states a sunset date is refused
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, give store-a (ga) a sunset date 30 days after today, and run stego registry compose.
then: Expects a non-zero exit and a message that names store-a and its sunset date.

title: Graduation to ga removes the sunset date
when: With ST-SUP-TD03, record the full quality bar for beta-x at its current digest, run stego registry graduate beta-x, then stego registry inspect beta-x.
then: Expects graduate to exit 0 and print ga, and inspect to show the stage ga and no sunset date.

title: Graduation to ga is refused for each missing piece of the bar, naming it
when: With ST-SUP-TD03, give beta-x the full bar at its current digest but one piece, and run stego registry graduate beta-x four times: without its security review, without its benchmark, without its design review, and without the conformance pass of the port it provides.
then: Expects each run to exit non-zero, name the one missing piece, and leave beta-x at beta.

title: Graduation to ga with no evidence names every missing piece at once
when: With ST-SUP-TD03, run stego registry graduate beta-x with no evidence recorded.
then: Expects a non-zero exit and a message that names the security review, the benchmark, the design review and the conformance pass, all four.

title: Evidence at an old digest does not count for graduation
when: With ST-SUP-TD03, record the full bar for beta-x, then change one generator file of beta-x so its digest moves, and run stego registry graduate beta-x.
then: Expects a non-zero exit and a message that names each of the four pieces as made at the old digest.

title: A component that provides two ports needs a conformance pass for each
when: With ST-SUP-TD03, let beta-x provide two ports, record the full bar with a conformance pass for the first port only, and run stego registry graduate beta-x.
then: Expects a non-zero exit and a message that names the second port and its suite, and not the first.

title: Graduation to ga with no reference comparison is refused
when: With ST-SUP-TD03, record for beta-x every piece of the bar except the reference comparison, and run stego registry graduate beta-x.
then: Expects a non-zero exit and a message that names the reference comparison as missing.

title: A reference comparison at an old contract set digest is stale
when: With ST-SUP-TD03, record the full bar for beta-x, then change one of its output contracts, and run stego registry graduate beta-x.
then: Expects a non-zero exit and a message that names the reference comparison as stale, with the old and the current digest of the contract set.

title: Graduation is refused while a promise is undecided, naming each undecided promise
when: With ST-SUP-TD03, record the full bar for beta-x with a reference comparison in which, of four promises, one is adopted with its contract, one declined with a reason, and two have no verdict; run stego registry graduate beta-x.
then: Expects a non-zero exit and a message that names both undecided promises, and neither of the decided ones.

title: A comparison that decides every promise lets the component graduate
when: With ST-SUP-TD03, record the full bar for beta-x with a reference comparison in which every promise is adopted with its contract or declined with a reason; run stego registry graduate beta-x.
then: Expects exit 0 and the stage ga.

title: A benchmark of free text only is refused, naming what a figure must hold
when: With ST-SUP-TD03, run stego registry evidence beta-x --kind benchmark with a file that holds only a paragraph of text.
then: Expects a non-zero exit and a message that says a figure needs a reference, a metric, a value, a unit and a better direction, with no evidence recorded.

title: A benchmark figure without its unit or its better direction is refused, naming the missing field
when: With ST-SUP-TD03, run stego registry evidence beta-x --kind benchmark with one figure that has no unit; then with one that has no better direction; then with one that has the better direction sideways.
then: Expects each run to exit non-zero and name the figure and the missing or wrong field.

title: A benchmark with no figure for one of its references is refused
when: With ST-SUP-TD03, run stego registry evidence beta-x --kind benchmark with figures against ref-1 only, where beta-x names ref-1 and ref-2.
then: Expects a non-zero exit and a message that names ref-2.

title: Each figure that regressed against the previous version is reported, and an improved one is not
when: With ST-SUP-TD03, record a benchmark of beta-x 0.2.0 with three figures: latency 10 ms (lower is better), throughput 500 requests per second (higher is better), memory 40 MiB (lower is better). Release 0.3.0 and record latency 12 ms, throughput 450 requests per second and memory 30 MiB.
then: Expects the second record to exit 0 and its output to name latency and throughput as regressed, each with both values, and not memory.
notes: One regression of each direction, so a comparison that reads every figure as lower is better fails the test.

title: Promotion copies the component at its exact digest, with the config schema, the ports, the slots, the output contracts and the generator unchanged
when: With ST-SUP-TD02, compute the component digest of local-a (stage beta) in the local registry, run stego registry promote local-a --to a checkout of the common registry, compare each file of local-a in the checkout with the file in the local registry, and compute the component digest of the copy.
then: Expects exit 0, and each file of the config schema, the ports, the slot contracts, the output contracts and the generator to have the same bytes as in the local registry; only the stage and the sunset differ. Expects the digest of the copy to equal the digest in the local registry.
notes: Decision on ST-SUP-Q02, reading a: the component digest leaves out the stage and the sunset (ST-GEN-DS01), so the copy at alpha keeps the digest of local-a at beta.

title: Promotion of a name that the common registry holds is refused, naming it
when: With ST-SUP-TD02, rename local-a to store-a in the local registry, and run stego registry promote store-a --to a checkout of the common registry.
then: Expects a non-zero exit, a message that names store-a, and no change in the checkout.

title: A promoted component enters at alpha, whatever its local stage
when: With ST-SUP-TD02, run stego registry promote local-a (beta) --to a checkout of the common registry; then, in a new checkout, promote local-a with its local stage set to ga.
then: Expects both copies to have the stage alpha.

title: Promotion changes only the given checkout, and makes no commit or push
when: With ST-SUP-TD02, record the commits of the common registry's repository and of the checkout, run stego registry promote local-a --to the checkout, and read git status and git log of both.
then: Expects the checkout to hold the copy as uncommitted changes, its HEAD to be the same commit, and the common registry's repository to have no new commit or ref.
notes: The review and the acceptance of the change are outside STEGO; this test proves that STEGO does not write to the common registry by itself.

title: A port with fields that have no meaning is refused, naming each field
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, run stego registry define-port on the folder of new-port with three fields: id with its meaning, and count and region with an empty meaning.
then: Expects a non-zero exit and a message that names count and region, and not id, with no port recorded.

title: A port that does not say what a provider undertakes is refused
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, run stego registry define-port on new-port with every field meaning and no statement of what a provider undertakes.
then: Expects a non-zero exit and a message that names new-port and what a provider undertakes as missing.

title: A port with no conformance suite is refused
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, run stego registry define-port on new-port with no conformance suite.
then: Expects a non-zero exit and a message that names new-port and its conformance suite as missing.

title: The first provider of a port whose suite is missing is refused at graduation, naming the port
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, define new-port with the suite conformance/new-port, then remove that folder; add new-a (beta) that provides new-port, record the rest of the bar, and run stego registry graduate new-a.
then: Expects a non-zero exit, a message that names new-port and its missing suite, and new-a left at beta.

title: Defining a port name that is already defined is refused, even with the same content
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, run stego registry define-port on a folder named store-port, once with the same content as the defined store-port and once with a changed meaning.
then: Expects both runs to exit non-zero and name store-port as already defined, with the port unchanged.

title: A changed meaning under a new port name is accepted
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, run stego registry define-port on store-port-v2, which is store-port with one changed field meaning.
then: Expects exit 0 and both store-port and store-port-v2 defined.

title: A provider with no conformance pass does not graduate, naming the port and the suite
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, add new-a (beta) that provides store-port, record its security review, benchmark, design review and reference comparison, and run stego registry graduate new-a.
then: Expects a non-zero exit, a message that names store-port and conformance/store-port, and new-a left at beta.

title: A conformance pass at an old digest does not count
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, add new-a (beta) with the full bar including a conformance pass of store-port, change one generator file of new-a, record the other pieces again at the new digest, and run stego registry graduate new-a.
then: Expects a non-zero exit and a message that names store-port, its suite and the old digest of the pass.

title: A slot whose contract file is missing is refused, naming the slot and the file
when: With ST-SUP-TD05, run stego registry declare-slot api-a after_create --contract slots/after_create.proto, a file that does not exist.
then: Expects a non-zero exit and a message that names after_create and slots/after_create.proto, with no slot declared.

title: A contract file that holds no service is refused, naming the slot and the file
when: With ST-SUP-TD05, run stego registry declare-slot api-a after_create --contract on the v2-noservice file.
then: Expects a non-zero exit and a message that names after_create, the file and that it holds no service.

title: Declaring a slot again with a contract that fails FILE rules is refused, naming the slot and each rule
when: With ST-SUP-TD05, run stego registry declare-slot api-a before_create --contract on the v2-breaking file.
then: Expects a non-zero exit and a message that names before_create and each FILE rule that fails: at least the rule for the changed field number and the rule for the removed method, as the pinned Buf names them.
notes: v2-breaking fails two rules, so a message that names only the first fails the test.

title: Releasing a component whose slot contract fails FILE rules is refused, naming the slot and each rule
when: With ST-SUP-TD05, put the v2-breaking contract at the path of before_create and run stego registry release api-a --version 1.1.0.
then: Expects a non-zero exit, a message that names before_create and each failing rule, and no version 1.1.0 recorded.

title: A breaking contract under a new slot name is accepted
when: With ST-SUP-TD05, run stego registry declare-slot api-a before_create_v2 --contract on the v2-breaking file, with a generator that invokes before_create_v2.
then: Expects exit 0 and both before_create and before_create_v2 offered by api-a.

title: A slot that no generator of its component invokes is refused, naming the slot and the component
when: With ST-SUP-TD05, run stego registry declare-slot api-a after_create --contract on a valid file, while no generator of api-a invokes after_create.
then: Expects a non-zero exit and a message that names after_create and api-a.

title: A fill built against the first contract of a slot compiles against each later contract
when: With ST-SUP-TD05, release api-a with v2-compatible, then with a v3 that adds a second method within the FILE rules; after each release, generate the example service with the fill built against v1 and run go build.
then: Expects go build to pass after each release, with the v1 fill unchanged.
notes: The build needs the Go SDK: the suite puts the pinned SDK in a local cache keyed by digest and runs the build on the developer workstation (ST-STD-LOCAL). The v1 fill does not implement the method that v3 adds, so the emitted code must let a fill leave a later method out; a test whose fill already implements every method misses this.

title: The search names every provider of a port with its stage
when: With ST-SUP-TD02, add store-b (ga) as a second provider of store-port, and run stego registry search --provides store-port; then run stego registry search --provides local-port.
then: Expects the first output to list store-a and store-b, in name order, each with ga, and the second to list local-a, from the local registry, with beta.

title: The search names every component that requires a port with its stage
when: With ST-SUP-TD02, add api-b (beta), which requires store-port, and run stego registry search --requires store-port.
then: Expects the output to list api-a with ga and api-b with beta, in name order, and no other component.

title: A default provider below ga is refused, naming the port and each provider with its stage and the suite it has not passed
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, add store-b (beta) and store-c (alpha), which both provide store-port-b and have no conformance pass, and run stego registry curate on svc-arch with store-b as the default provider of store-port-b.
then: Expects a non-zero exit and a message that names store-port-b, store-b with beta and store-c with alpha, and for each the conformance suite of store-port-b as not passed.
notes: Two providers, so a message that names only the chosen default fails the test. Both are below ga, because ST-SUP-INV03 does not let a component below ga provide a port that a ga component provides.

title: A ga default provider is accepted
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, add store-b (ga, with the full bar) as a second provider of store-port, and run stego registry curate on svc-arch with store-b as the default of store-port.
then: Expects exit 0 and output that prints store-b as the provider of store-port.

title: A ga archetype without a default concern is refused, naming each missing one
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, run stego registry curate on svc-arch at ga without tenancy, then without audit-log, then without both.
then: Expects each run to exit non-zero and name the missing component; the third names both tenancy and audit-log.

title: A curated ga archetype records tenancy and audit-log as its default concerns
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, run stego registry curate on svc-arch at ga, then stego registry inspect svc-arch, and then stego plan of its example declaration.
then: Expects inspect to list tenancy and audit-log as the default concerns of svc-arch, and the active component set of the plan to hold both.

title: An opt-out with a reason is recorded with the service
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, write a declaration of svc-arch that opts out of audit-log with the reason "audit is kept by the caller", and run stego apply.
then: Expects exit 0, audit-log not in the active component set, the generation record of the service to name audit-log and the reason, and no file of the registry to change.
notes: Decision on ST-SUP-Q03, reading a: the reason is kept with the service (ST-SUP-INV15, ST-GEN-EN01 field Defaults left).

title: An opt-out with an empty reason or with no reason is refused, naming the component
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, write a declaration of svc-arch that opts out of tenancy with an empty reason, then one with no reason, and run stego validate each time.
then: Expects each run to exit non-zero and name tenancy.

title: Binding a mixin without the mixin it requires is refused, naming both
when: With ST-SUP-TD01 and the mixins durable-events and kafka-events, where kafka-events requires durable-events, write a declaration that binds kafka-events alone, and run stego validate.
then: Expects a non-zero exit and a message that names kafka-events and durable-events.

title: Binding a mixin with the mixin it requires is accepted
when: With ST-SUP-TD01 and both mixins, write a declaration that binds kafka-events and durable-events, and run stego validate.
then: Expects exit 0.

title: Binding event-publisher gives durable-events and kafka-events
when: With the shipped registry, runs stego apply for ST-DECL-TD02 with the mixin event-publisher, for it with the mixins durable-events and kafka-events, and for it with no mixin.
then: Expects the two applies to make the same generated files with the same content, but for the digest of the declaration's text, and both to add the Kafka destination to the outbox and to the commands, which a plan with no mixin does not have.
notes: Level: integration, through the stego binary. The version of the declaration is the digest of its text, which names the mixins in two ways, so the test leaves it out. The base of rest-crud has the outbox already, so the test checks the Kafka destination that the alias adds. Mutation caught: kafka-events adds no component. The orchestrator decided option (c) on 2026-11-13 under the Product owner's delegation: event-publisher is a true alias, and durable-events keeps the proto package and the contract of the slot.

title: Binding event-publisher gives a notice that names both mixins and the sunset date
when: With the shipped registry, run stego validate for a declaration that binds event-publisher.
then: Expects exit 0 and one notice in the output of validate that names durable-events, kafka-events and the sunset date of event-publisher as the shipped registry states it.
notes: The test reads the sunset from the shipped registry, not from a constant. Mutation caught: the notice of the declaration, which cannot know the date. The orchestrator decided option (b) of ST-SUP-Q117 on 2026-11-13 under the Product owner's delegation: the alias states deprecated_on and sunset as dates in its mixin.yaml, and the registry refuses a sunset that is not deprecated_on plus the ga window of registry/policy.yaml in months.

title: An alias binds only the mixins that the archetype allows, and a mixin needs the mixins it requires
when: Adds to a test registry the mixins store-m and send-m, which requires store-m, and the alias pub of both, and reconciles the alias with an archetype that allows pub and store-m, then with one that allows all three, and then send-m alone.
then: Expects the first refused, naming send-m as not compatible, the second taken, and the third refused, naming send-m and store-m.
notes: Mutations caught: no expansion of the alias; the compatibility of the declared names only; no check of a required mixin. The orchestrator decided option (c) on 2026-11-13 under the Product owner's delegation: event-publisher is a true alias, and durable-events keeps the proto package and the contract of the slot.

title: A registry refuses an alias of an alias, of a mixin it does not hold, or that adds anything
when: Loads registries with an alias of an alias, an alias of itself, an alias of a missing mixin, an alias that adds a component, and a plain alias of two mixins.
then: Expects each of the first four refused with its fault, and the plain alias loaded with its two mixins.
notes: Mutation caught: no refusal of an alias of an alias, so no loop can form. The orchestrator decided option (c) on 2026-11-13 under the Product owner's delegation: event-publisher is a true alias, and durable-events keeps the proto package and the contract of the slot.

title: A registry holds a deprecated alias to its sunset and to the slot contracts of its mixins
when: Loads registries with an alias of a mixin with a slot: with no policy file, with no sunset, with no deprecated_on, with a sunset that is not one ga window after deprecated_on, with a ga window of 3 months, with no copy of the slot contract, with a copy that differs, and with dates on a mixin that is no alias; then a registry where the alias is deprecated on 2026-08-31 with the sunset 2027-02-28, a ga window of 6 months and a copy of the contract.
then: Expects each of the first eight refused with its fault, the wrong sunsets refused with the sunset the policy gives, and the last loaded with the sunset 2027-02-28: a month shorter than the day gives its last day.
notes: Mutations caught: no rule of the sunset; the month added by the calendar overflow of Go, which gives 2027-03-03; no check of the copy; a check of its presence only. A copy of the contract keeps the contract digest of a fill that names the slot by the alias, which a contract path of the target would move. The orchestrator decided option (b) of ST-SUP-Q117 on 2026-11-13 under the Product owner's delegation: the alias states deprecated_on and sunset as dates in its mixin.yaml, and the registry refuses a sunset that is not deprecated_on plus the ga window of registry/policy.yaml in months.

title: A default concern below ga is refused, naming the component and its stage
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, set tenancy to beta, and run stego registry curate on svc-arch at ga.
then: Expects a non-zero exit and a message that names tenancy and beta.

title: A component with a runtime provider names the runtime package that holds it
when: Run stego registry inspect spicedb-authz with the shipped registry, and list the packages of the runtime library at the version that its archetype pins.
then: Expects inspect to name the runtime package of the provider of authz-decision, and that package to be in the runtime library at the pinned version.

title: A component with a runtime provider emits only files that vary with the declaration
when: With ST-SUP-TD04, run stego plan for each of the two declarations with spicedb-authz, and compare each file of spicedb-authz after the module path and the package name are normalised.
then: Expects every file that spicedb-authz emits to differ between the two plans.

title: A static file is refused, naming the file and the runtime package it belongs in
when: With ST-SUP-TD01 and ST-SUP-TD04, run stego registry add on authz-copy, which provides authz-decision, names a runtime package, and emits the provider as a file that is the same for both declarations.
then: Expects a non-zero exit and a message that names authz-copy, the static file and the runtime package.

title: A runtime provider with a conformance pass at the component's digest graduates
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, add authz-b (beta), which provides authz-decision from the runtime library, record its conformance pass with stego registry evidence --kind conformance and the other pieces of the bar at its digest, and run stego registry graduate authz-b.
then: Expects the evidence run to print the pass as port conformance at the current digest, and graduate to exit 0 with ga.

title: A runtime provider with no conformance pass at the component's digest does not graduate
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, add authz-b (beta) with every piece of the bar but the conformance pass, and run stego registry graduate authz-b.
then: Expects a non-zero exit and a message that names authz-decision and its suite.

title: A component that imports the provider at another runtime library version is refused, naming both versions
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, run stego registry add on authz-b, whose emitted code imports the runtime library at a version other than the one svc-arch pins.
then: Expects a non-zero exit and a message that names authz-b, the imported version and the pinned version.

title: The emitted code requires the runtime library at the pinned version
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, run stego apply for a declaration of svc-arch with authz-b, and read go.mod.
then: Expects go.mod to require the runtime library at exactly the version svc-arch pins.

title: Retiring a component removes it from the active registry
when: With ST-SUP-TD03, run stego registry retire beta-x, then stego registry compose and stego registry search --provides on the port of beta-x.
then: Expects retire to exit 0 and print beta-x as retired, compose not to list beta-x, and search to list no beta-x.

title: Retiring a component names every recorded service that uses it
when: With ST-SUP-TD03, run stego registry retire beta-x with the consumer records of the four checkouts available.
then: Expects the output to name svc-one and svc-two, and not svc-three or svc-four.
notes: ST-SUP-CLI12 takes no checkout today; the builder gives retire the consumer records, by checkouts as in ST-SUP-CLI18 or from the read model ST-SUP-RM03.

title: A missed sunset is reported for every service that still uses the component
when: With ST-SUP-TD03, add svc-five, which also uses beta-old with no acceptance, and run stego registry sunsets with the five checkouts.
then: Expects a non-zero exit and output that names svc-four and svc-five, each with beta-old and its sunset date, and no other service.

title: Checking fails in each service that uses a component past its sunset, naming the sunset
when: With ST-SUP-TD03, add svc-five, which also uses beta-old with no acceptance, and run stego validate in svc-four and then in svc-five.
then: Expects each run to exit non-zero and give a message that names beta-old as past its sunset, with its sunset date.
notes: svc-four also has no acceptance of beta-old, so validate also refuses it under ST-DECL-INV14; a test that checks only the exit status passes on that refusal alone. The test must find the sunset fault itself in the message of each service.

title: No missed sunset gives no report and exit 0
when: With ST-SUP-TD03, remove svc-four, and run stego registry sunsets with the other three checkouts.
then: Expects exit 0 and no service named.
